lessons.title: Stance, Evidence, and the Subjunctive
lessons.learn: Calibrate assertion, doubt, and evaluation in extended professional and academic discourse.

grammar.title: Mood and evidential stance
grammar.explain: The indicative asserts within the discourse frame; the subjunctive after doubt, necessity, and evaluation presents content as non-asserted or evaluated. Lexical hedges further calibrate commitment.

examples.r: le do-ne les pɑ̃-se kə la mə-zyr a y œ̃ e-fe li-mi-te
examples.en: The data suggest that the measure had a limited effect.

lessons.title: Reported Discourse and Tense Sequence
lessons.learn: Report competing voices while preserving temporal viewpoint and attribution.

grammar.title: Indirect speech and tense concordance
grammar.explain: Reported discourse can shift tense and deixis according to the reporting frame. A C1 synthesis identifies who owns each claim and avoids turning reported allegations into facts.

lessons.title: Professional Diplomacy and Conditional Politeness
lessons.learn: Manage disagreement, requests, and deadlines with precise interpersonal force.

grammar.title: Conditional mitigation
grammar.explain: The conditional softens requests and proposals; imperfect and pluperfect forms construct distance or unreal alternatives. Mitigation must not hide who should do what by when.
grammar.pattern: Serait-il possible de + infinitive / que + subjunctive

examples.r: ʒə vu so-re gre də trɑ̃s-mɛtr la vɛr-sjɔ̃ re-vi-ze a-vɑ̃ ʒø-di

lessons.title: Academic Cohesion and Qualified Comparison
lessons.learn: Define terms, compare compatible evidence, and guide readers through dense exposition.

grammar.title: Nominalisation and qualification
grammar.explain: French academic prose uses nominalisation and explicit metadiscourse, but responsible writing keeps agents and evidence limits recoverable. Reformulation preserves scope.

lessons.title: Idiomatic Register and Francophone Variation
lessons.learn: Interpret idioms and register across settings without reducing Francophone usage to a single norm.

grammar.title: Register and regional adequacy
grammar.explain: Lexicon, pronunciation, address, and idiom vary across Francophone communities. Label region and genre, distinguish comprehension from chosen production norm, and avoid treating variation as error.

lessons.title: Synthesis and Audience Mediation
lessons.learn: Relate conflicting sources and reformulate specialist content for another audience.

grammar.title: Source integration
grammar.explain: A synthesis compares methods, scopes, and certainty rather than stacking summaries. Mediation changes density and terminology without altering the source’s modal force.
grammar.pattern: source A + source B relation + qualified synthesis

examples.t: Les études convergent sur la direction de l’effet, mais divergent sur son ampleur.
examples.r: le ze-tyd kɔ̃-vɛrʒ syr la di-rɛk-sjɔ̃ də le-fɛ mɛ di-vɛrʒ syr sɔ̃ nɑ̃-plœr
examples.en: The studies converge on the direction of the effect but diverge on its magnitude.

examples.t: La synthèse conserve les réserves méthodologiques propres à chaque source.
examples.r: la sɛ̃-tɛz kɔ̃-sɛrv le re-zɛrv me-to-do-lo-ʒik propr a ʃak surs
examples.en: The synthesis preserves the methodological caveats specific to each source.

examples.t: La version publique reformule le constat sans le transformer en certitude.
examples.r: la vɛr-sjɔ̃ py-blik rə-for-myl lə kɔ̃-sta sɑ̃ lə trɑ̃s-for-me ɑ̃ sɛr-ti-tyd
examples.en: The public version reformulates the finding without turning it into certainty.

mistakes: Preserve mood, stance, cohesion, and register; a grammatically possible form may still be pragmatically inappropriate.
